subject: Colts release Daniel Jones
title: Colts release Daniel Jones: Why, and who starts at QB now?
answer: On Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, Indianapolis Colts coach Shane Steichen announced the team is releasing quarterback Daniel Jones and starting Anthony Richardson Sr. The move came the day after a 26-3 loss at Houston dropped the Colts to 3-8.
in_the_news: Jones signed a two-year, $88 million deal this offseason, so cutting him 11 games in is a costly admission that the plan failed. Richardson, the No. 4 overall pick in 2023, gets his first start since the 2024 season.
body:
Jones started all 11 games this season, completing 205 of 351 passes (58.4%) for 1,974 yards, seven touchdowns and a career-high 13 interceptions. Against Houston on Thursday night he went 12 of 27 for 144 yards and an interception before he was pulled for Richardson. Asked whether Jones had asked to be let go, Steichen said: "No. This was a decision that was just made for the best interest of both parties." On the timing, he added, "It's just where we're at in our season." Jones, 29, came to Indianapolis in 2025 after his release by the New York Giants, and his first Colts season ended with a torn Achilles tendon.

What a release means, in plain terms: because the trade deadline has passed, Jones goes on waivers first. Any of the other 31 teams can claim him through 4 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 23, but a claiming team would take on his contract, including $2 million for the rest of this season and $38 million in non-guaranteed money for 2027, according to CBS Sports. Analysts expect no claim, which would make him a free agent who can sign anywhere for a smaller deal. For the Colts, CBS Sports and Bleacher Report put the dead-money charge at about $35.2 million on next season's salary cap if he clears.

Richardson has appeared in only two games this season. In 19 career games, 15 of them starts, he has completed 50.6% of his passes for 2,408 yards with 11 touchdown passes and 13 interceptions, and run for 640 yards and 10 touchdowns. His last start came in Week 16 of the 2024 season.

Next up: Richardson is set to start Sunday, Nov. 29, when the Colts host the New York Giants, Jones's first NFL team. Fantasy players who rostered Jones should look elsewhere for now; his next job depends on whether a contender with an injured starter calls after he clears waivers.

faq.q: Why did the Colts release Daniel Jones?
faq.a: The offense stalled during a 3-8 start, and Jones led the NFL in turnovers. Coach Shane Steichen called it a decision made in the best interest of both parties.

faq.q: Who is the Colts' starting quarterback now?
faq.a: Anthony Richardson Sr., starting with the Nov. 29, 2026, home game against the New York Giants.

faq.q: Can Daniel Jones sign with another team?
faq.a: Yes, after waivers. Teams can claim him through 4 p.m. ET on Monday, Nov. 23. If no one claims him, he becomes a free agent.

faq.q: How much does releasing Jones cost the Colts?
faq.a: CBS Sports and Bleacher Report estimate about $35.2 million in dead money against the Colts' 2027 salary cap if he clears waivers.
